title: How to Automate Inbound Lead Qualification and Warm Transfers on Your Existing Phone System
summary: Learn how to qualify inbound leads with AI voice agents, connect to an existing phone system and CRM, and transfer callers to staff with context.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


- Qualify inbound sales calls with approved questions and eligibility rules, then confirm the CRM result and pass the caller’s verified context to a rep. Your existing phone system needs tested routes into the AI agent, to a staffed queue, and to a no-answer fallback.
- Test changed intent, early requests for a person, failed CRM writes, and unavailable reps. Check what the receiving rep hears or can read at pickup.
- SigmaMind AI documents[conversation branches](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/documentation/agents/add-basic-nodes/branch-node) and[tool actions](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/documentation/agents/add-advance-nodes/app-action-node) . The example’s eligibility rules, CRM permissions, queue checks, and handoff details require deployment-specific design and testing.
- See the[broader inbound workflow guide](https://sigmamind.ai/blog/inbound-voice-ai-workflows-human-handoff) ,[vendor comparison](https://sigmamind.ai/blog/inbound-call-automation-comparison) , and[warm-transfer overview](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/warm-transfer) for adjacent decisions.


## What "qualifying on your existing phone system" actually requires


To keep qualification visible in your existing queues and reports, verify how your phone system routes calls to the AI agent and records their return. A separate AI call path may leave gaps in contact-center visibility.[Teneo’s vendor-selection guide](https://www.teneo.ai/blog/conversational-ai-vendor-selection-guide-2026) raises this concern for some SIP transfer paths, but your reporting needs to be checked against the route you actually use. Before configuring questions, check how calls reach the AI agent, how they return to a staffed queue, and which system records each stage.


SigmaMind AI documents[an optional inbound webhook](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/documentation/calls/receive-calls) for numbers purchased or imported into its platform. The webhook receives an inbound_call event and can return variables or select an agent. Those call-arrival options do not, by themselves, establish a connection to your current phone system or confirm that queue availability is visible to the AI agent. Verify the route into SigmaMind AI, the route back to your staffed queue, and whether the AI agent can obtain queue-availability information in your deployment.


The qualification flow also needs access to the right CRM data without granting broader write permissions than the task requires. SigmaMind AI documents[Tool Actions](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/documentation/agents/add-advance-nodes/app-action-node) for external app calls and a[Branch node](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/documentation/agents/add-basic-nodes/branch-node) for routing decisions. You define the approved questions, eligibility rules, consent and verification checks, CRM field mapping, and response to a failed write. Confirm that a receiving rep can access the verified answers before treating a transfer as a complete handoff.


## Walking one inbound sales call end to end


Consider a caller asking about a service purchase. The example below follows that call through qualification and a possible transfer, including a change of intent or an early request for a person. The eligibility rules, CRM access, phone-system routes, and fallback are illustrative configuration, not documented SigmaMind AI behavior.


### Call arrives and intent is captured


In this example, the existing phone system routes a sales call to a number configured to receive calls through SigmaMind AI. The[inbound call documentation](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/documentation/calls/receive-calls) says an optional number-level webhook can receive an inbound_call event with the caller and dialed numbers, then return variables or select an agent. Without a webhook, the call connects to the assigned agent. Test how your existing phone system sends calls to that number and receives transfers back. The webhook documentation does not establish queue or transfer behavior for your phone system.


After the greeting, the agent asks what the caller needs and waits for an answer. SigmaMind AI[recommends analyzing voice intent](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/documentation/agents/agent-builder-overview) with an Analyze Customer Message node after the caller speaks, rather than filtering voice calls at the Start Trigger. If the caller describes a sales inquiry, the illustrative flow proceeds to the approved qualifying questions.


If the caller asks for a person immediately, the flow should skip those questions and attempt the human route you have configured and tested. The caller should not have to claim a sales intent first. If no rep can take the call, your configured fallback should tell the caller what happens next rather than returning them to the qualification script.


### Asking only the approved qualifying questions


Configure and test the assistant to ask only approved questions, and stop those questions when the caller changes intent. In an illustrative sales intake, you might permit questions about the caller’s intended purchase, location, and timeframe. Ask only what your eligibility rules require, accept “I don’t know,” and send requests outside that scope to a person. Your implementation must enforce those limits. SigmaMind AI documents[conversation analysis and branching building blocks](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/documentation/agents/agent-builder-overview) , not a ready-made qualification template with enforced question limits.


Set a disclosure and consent policy before questioning. For this example, the assistant identifies itself as automated, asks whether the caller is willing to continue, and explains how to reach a person. Confirm the legal requirements that apply to your callers and location rather than treating this example as a universal requirement. If a caller declines, stop the questions and follow your human-routing policy.


Recheck intent as the caller answers. A caller who first asks about buying service may then clarify that they need help with an existing account. The flow should stop the sales questions and route the revised request rather than finish a script that no longer fits. Record answers already given as caller statements, but do not treat them as a completed eligibility decision.


### Deciding eligibility and recording the result


The[Branch node](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/documentation/agents/add-basic-nodes/branch-node) can decide whether a caller meets your approved eligibility criteria using conditions, session variables, or results returned by another system. For example, you might require a supported service area and a qualifying project type. Your operation defines those rules and decides which answers need independent verification. A caller’s statement should remain marked as self-reported unless a trusted source confirms it.


In a configured integration, a qualified result could trigger a[Tool Action](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/documentation/agents/add-advance-nodes/app-action-node) to send the outcome and recorded answers to your CRM, with each answer marked as self-reported or independently verified. You must define the field mapping, obtain any required consent, and give the integration appropriate write permissions. Confirm that the CRM accepted the record before telling the caller it was saved. If the write fails, preserve the available call context for a human and flag the missing record rather than presenting the update as complete.


An unqualified result should follow your approved alternative, such as a clear explanation or a different destination. If an answer is missing or conflicting, route the uncertain result for human review instead of treating the caller as qualified. A business-hours rule can indicate when a queue is scheduled to be staffed, but it cannot confirm that a rep is available now. Check live availability through a verified integration or use a tested no-answer fallback; neither should change the eligibility decision.


### Warm transfer with confirmed context


Before bridging the call, check the caller’s current intent and the answers used in the eligibility decision. Identify which answers the caller supplied and which your systems verified. If the workflow requires consent, verification, or a CRM write, check each result rather than treating an attempted action as complete. If your phone system exposes queue availability through a verified integration, use it to avoid sending the caller to an unstaffed queue. Otherwise, test a no-answer fallback. SigmaMind AI’s published warm-transfer overview does not document built-in rep presence detection.


[SigmaMind AI describes a handoff](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/warm-transfer) that prepares a structured conversation summary and passes variables covering intent and responses. Its private whisper can brief the receiving rep before the bridge, while an optional three-way announcement can introduce the transfer once the call connects. For this sales call, configure and test the whisper to give the rep the caller’s current intent, the relevant answers and their verification status, and any unresolved question. The overview does not specify exact field names or promise a CRM screen pop. Test what the rep actually receives on your phone system before relying on either.


### No answer and fallback handling


If the receiving rep does not answer, the call needs a defined next destination.[SigmaMind AI’s warm-transfer overview](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/warm-transfer) describes retry logic and fallbacks, but it does not specify retry counts or no-answer routing. You should decide how your existing phone system handles this case and test it before sending live calls through the flow.


An illustrative fallback could try the next available rep, then offer a callback queue or voicemail if your operation supports those options. Each route needs its own availability check. Test whether the caller stays connected, whether the next rep receives the qualification context, and whether a callback request reaches an authorized queue. If every route fails, tell the caller that no one is available and give a next step you can actually support, such as calling back during staffed hours.


## Check what the receiving rep gets


Use a test call to establish what the receiving rep hears and can read before the caller joins. SigmaMind AI’s[warm-transfer overview](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/warm-transfer) describes a structured conversation summary, intent and response variables, and a private whisper, but it does not specify how those details appear in your phone system or CRM.


- **Described in the overview.** Test whether the rep receives the summary, current caller intent, and responses on your route. Record what the rep hears in the whisper separately from what the rep can read.
- **Needed for qualification.** Check whether the rep receives the answers used in the eligibility decision, their verification status, the decision itself, and any unresolved question. The overview does not specify field names or a delivery format for those details.
- **Not confirmed.** Test whether consent and verification status reach the rep. Check the CRM record directly if the rep needs to know whether a write succeeded. Do not assume an automatic screen pop or CRM update.
- **At pickup.** Have a rep identify any missing facts before you rely on the handoff for live sales calls.


## Vendor checklist and scenario-based acceptance tests


Ask each vendor to demonstrate the qualification call through a test route on your existing phone system, rather than relying only on a standalone demo number. Check whether your call reports show the AI-handled portion, the transfer, and the final disposition. A[vendor-selection guide](https://www.teneo.ai/blog/conversational-ai-vendor-selection-guide-2026) warns that some SIP transfer paths can leave gaps in contact-center reporting. Request the vendor’s uptime commitment, incident response terms, and evidence of how unanswered transfers appear in your reports.


Test CRM access with the permissions you plan to grant. The vendor should show which fields the AI can read or write, how it confirms a write succeeded, and what the rep receives when the CRM is unavailable. Ask for a call trace that lets you match the confirmed answers, eligibility decision, CRM result, and handoff without assuming a screen pop.


Run the same six calls against every candidate, using the same phone-system routes, CRM permissions, and test data. Set your own pass criteria before testing. Record the caller and rep experience alongside the call trace and CRM result.


- **False qualification.** Have a caller initially give an eligible answer, then change it to an ineligible one before transfer. Check whether the AI updates the decision and avoids routing the caller as qualified.
- **Missing handoff context.** Have a caller qualify for a sales transfer, then request account support before the bridge. Check whether the flow changes destination and whether the receiving rep gets the current intent, relevant answers, and their verification status.
- **Failed CRM write.** Deny write permission or simulate an outage. Check whether the AI avoids claiming the record was saved, flags the failure in the trace, and passes available details to the rep through an authorized route.
- **Transfer failure.** Make the intended queue unavailable. Check whether the caller reaches your configured fallback, remains informed of the next step, and has a call record showing the attempted transfer and outcome.
- **Early request for a person.** Ask for a rep before answering a qualifying question. Check whether the AI stops questioning, follows the human route, and uses the no-answer fallback if needed.
- **Consent or verification limit.** Decline consent or fail a required verification step. Check whether the AI stops the restricted action, avoids an unauthorized CRM write, and routes the call according to your policy.


Use the[inbound vendor comparison](https://sigmamind.ai/blog/inbound-call-automation-comparison) for a broader vendor review and the[warm-transfer overview](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/warm-transfer) for handoff fundamentals.
